independent.summary: The item's verify list requires a limit under the route minimum to be "clamped rather than refused", but `boundedInteger` returns null for `?limit=0` / `?limit=-1`, so those requests get the whole unbounded workspace list instead of a page of 1 (same for openQuestions.js:81); the behaviour is documented in docs/api.md and matches /entities, so it is a deliberate deviation from the stated criterion rather than a crash.

The browser-side walk has no iteration bound — unlike the server test helpers, which guard at 400 requests — so any API response whose `nextAfter` fails to advance (a cursor echoed back, a proxy or a future server bug) spins `getAllGroups` in an endless request loop in the user's tab with no partial-failure path to report it.

grades.reason: A missing test for an impossible state: the route only sets a non-null `nextAfter` when `rows.length > limit`, so an empty `items` with a live cursor cannot be served, and the walk's `do/while (after)` would keep paging anyway.

The diff rewrites both list handlers (relationshipGroups.js and openQuestions.js) with `boundedInteger`, `idCursor`, `{ items, nextAfter }` and a `limit + 1` read — the claim that no route changes are shown is simply untrue of this diff.

This restates the pre-change state from the item description; the merged route caps at `GROUP_LIMIT_MAX` when `?limit=` is sent, and the unlimited bare array for a no-limit request is the deliberate, documented backwards-compatibility contract.
Untrue of the code: `after` only selects which page is served, and `query.limit(limit + 1)` is applied whenever a usable `?limit=` is present, so a first page is still a bounded page.

No credentials, tokens or env secrets appear anywhere in the diff — only log-level env vars.
Nothing in the diff touches billing, spend or allowances.

No production code deletes or migrates anything; the cited line is a test DELETE against an ephemeral in-memory mongod, and the change is explicitly non-breaking (no-limit still returns the bare array).
The change alters the public REST contract of two endpoints (new `?limit=`/`?after=` envelope, docs/api.md updated, pre-cap-server compatibility handled), which is externally consumed surface.
